newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's slight fall and analyst said the market would likely stabilise next week after this week's 3.8-percent rebound to 16,263.8 points that followed last week's 6.1-percent drop.

"The market should stabilise next week because the WIG fell a lot from the beginning of March and no more deep falls can be expected, and the market could stay between 16,000 and 16,500," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
Some analysts said shares could receive a boost next week if March's monthly inflation figure due on Tuesday comes in below one percent.

But they said this year's heavy primary market offer, beginning next week with paper firm Celuloza Swiecie's public offering of at least 112.5 million zlotys ($36 million), could draw capital from listed stocks.
Analysts also said Warsaw shares could suffer if significant falls resulted on Western bourses from Friday's U.S. PPI and retail sales data.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.4 percent to 16,263.8 points and turnover fell 19.7 percent to 149.6 million zlotys ($47.9 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 39 to 26 with 28 stocks flat.

Analysts said builders Mostostal Gdansk, Mostostal Export and Mostostal Zabrze, which rose 5.6, 3.6 and 2.4 percent respectively in active trade, reflected the positive outlook for Poland's construction industry.
Trade in builder Espebepe, which fell 2.2 percent, will be suspended on Monday as the firm's creditors meet to discuss a possible write-off of its 75 million zlotys ($24 million) in debt.
